docRequirement: desktop-scheduled-tasks.md:74 (§ Missed runs) binds the durable scheduler to a start/wake sweep: "When the app starts or your computer wakes, Desktop checks whether each task missed any runs in the last seven days. If it did, Desktop starts exactly one catch-up run for the most recently missed time and discards anything older. A daily task that missed six days runs once on wake. Desktop shows a notification when a catch-up run starts." So: a per-task cursor of the last fired occurrence, a seven-day window, exactly ONE fire per task at the most recent missed occurrence, everything older discarded, and a notification on that fire. :70 ("If your computer sleeps through a scheduled time, the run is skipped") governs the in-session minute tick, not the wake sweep.
current: Nessy's durable analogue is the Automations subsystem, and it has no cursor, no sweep and no wake trigger. (1) The clock: `SchedulerService.start()` (packages/shared/src/scheduler/scheduler-service.ts:33-45) computes `msUntilNextMinute` (:38), then `setTimeout` → first `tick()` at :42 and `setInterval(() => this.tick(), 60_000)` at :43. The first tick is at the next minute boundary; there is no immediate tick and no replay of anything before it. `tick()` (:58-87) builds a payload from `new Date()` only (:66-76). (2) The trigger predicate: `matchesBasePredicate` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:286-302) for `SchedulerTick` is exactly `return !!matcher.cron && matchesCron(matcher.cron, matcher.timezone);` (:289), and `matchesCron` (packages/shared/src/automations/cron-matcher.ts:25-57) asks only whether croner's `nextRun` from `startOfMinute - 1000` lands inside the current minute (:36-51). No cursor is read, no argument for "as of" time exists. (3) Nothing upstream compensates: `AutomationSystem` starts the scheduler in its constructor (packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.ts:162-164 → `startScheduler()` :393-407), and the tick callback only re-emits `SchedulerTick` on the event bus (:396-403). `PromptHandler.handleEvent` (packages/shared/src/automations/handlers/prompt-handler.ts:46-124) is a pure current-event path: matchers in (:52), `matcherMatches` (:63), prompts out (:120-123). (4) History is display-only: `appendAutomationHistoryEntry` (packages/shared/src/automations/history-store.ts:57-74) writes `{id, ts, ok, …}` (packages/shared/src/automations/webhook-utils.ts:62-77) where `ts = Date.now()` of the RUN; the `automations:getLastExecuted` handler (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/automations.ts:409-425) folds it to `id → ts`, and the only consumer is the UI label and sort (apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useAutomations.ts:54-64, apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/AutomationsListPanel.tsx:138-146, :240-243). It is also compacted away — 20 per matcher / 1000 global (packages/shared/src/automations/constants.ts:17,20). No scheduling code reads it. (5) No wake hook: `grep -arn powerMonitor` over the whole tree excluding node_modules returns only the doc-sweep JSON, zero source hits. The scheduler is created once per workspace inside `SessionManager.setupConfigWatcher` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:6931, `enableScheduler: true` at :7086) and never re-swept. (6) No notification on a scheduled fire: `showNotification` (apps/electron/src/main/notifications.ts:54) has no automation/catch-up caller.
divergence: The whole missed-run mechanism is absent, not narrowed: no persisted per-task last-occurrence cursor, no start-time sweep, no wake trigger, no seven-day window, no discard-older rule, no catch-up notification. Two specifics that shape the fix. (a) It is not enough to make the sweep re-emit `SchedulerTick`: `matchesBasePredicate` (utils.ts:289) evaluates the cron against the CURRENT minute, so a replayed tick matches nothing — the sweep needs its own matcher-selection path, not a synthetic tick. (b) The nearest existing timestamp, automation history `ts` (webhook-utils.ts:65), is the RUN time, not the scheduled occurrence, and is capped at 20 entries per matcher; using it as the cursor would double-fire or silently skip. The cursor must be the OCCURRENCE time and must live in its own durable file. The sibling session-scoped Cron tier already has the correct discipline and the correct reason written down (packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.ts:144-165: stamp at delivery, not enqueue; packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-scheduler.ts:121-131), but it implements the opposite contract (scheduled-tasks.md:215 forbids per-interval catch-up), is per-session and non-durable, and explicitly is not `SchedulerService` (session-cron-service.ts:9-16) — so it supplies a pattern to copy, not the behaviour.

change.what: Add `AUTOMATIONS_SCHEDULE_STATE_FILE = 'automations-schedule-state.json'` next to the existing file-name constants (:2-8) and `AUTOMATION_CATCHUP_WINDOW_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` carrying the doc quote for the seven-day window (desktop-scheduled-tasks.md:74).

Durable per-matcher cursor keyed by matcher id, value `{ lastFiredOccurrence: number }` — the OCCURRENCE epoch ms, never the run time. Lives at `join(workspaceRootPath, AUTOMATIONS_SCHEDULE_STATE_FILE)`; `workspaceRootPath` is the managed workspace dir (packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:50), the same directory as automations.json and automations-history.jsonl. Write atomically temp+rename at mode 0600, copying packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-cleanup.ts:196-203,270-274. Corrupt/missing file reads as empty (no cursor) — a first-run empty state must NOT fire everything, so the planner treats a missing cursor as `now` for that matcher on the very first sweep and persists it.

New export beside `matchesCron` (:25) wrapping croner's `new Cron(expr, opts).previousRuns(1, before)` (signature at node_modules/croner/dist/croner.d.ts:564) and returning epoch ms or null. Do not change `matchesCron` — it has six callers including packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/plugin-monitor-service.ts and pinned tests (cron-matcher.test.ts).

change.symbol: planCatchupFires({ matchers, state, now, windowMs }) (new file, pure)
change.what: For each `SchedulerTick` matcher with `matcher.enabled !== false` and a `cron`: `occ = previousOccurrence(cron, timezone, now)`; fire iff `occ !== null && occ > cursor && occ >= now - windowMs`. Emit at most ONE fire per matcher and return the new cursor = `occ` (that single value is how "discards anything older" is implemented — a daily task that missed six days yields one fire and one cursor jump). Pure and table-tested; mirror the reasoning comment style of packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-scheduler.ts:121-131.

Factor the per-matcher prompt build (:65-117: action filter, `deriveAutomationName`, `buildEnvFromPayload`, `expandEnvVars`, `parsePromptReferences`) into an exported function taking an explicit matcher list, so the catch-up sweep produces identical `PendingPrompt`s without going through `matcherMatches`. `handleEvent` keeps its matching and calls the extracted function.

New public `runMissedRunSweep(now = Date.now())`: read schedule state, call `planCatchupFires` over `getMatchersForEvent('SchedulerTick')`, build prompts via the extracted helper, hand them to `this.options.onPromptsReady` with a `catchUp: true` marker on `PendingPrompt`, then persist the new cursors. Call it once from `startScheduler()` (:393-407) before `this.scheduler.start()` (:405) — that is the "app starts" half — and leave it callable for the wake half. Also stamp the cursor on the NORMAL tick path (in the same place the tick's matches are known) so a run that already happened while the app was open is not replayed on the next start.

Public method iterating `this.automationSystems` (populated at :7082-7086) and calling `runMissedRunSweep()` on each, so the wake trigger has one entry point. In the existing `onPromptsReady` branch, when `pending.catchUp` is set, fire the desktop notification and mark the created session as catch-up in `triggeredBy` so the sidebar and history can say so. Add the method to packages/server-core/src/handlers/session-manager-interface.ts:349's neighbourhood if it must be reachable over RPC.

Inside the `app.whenReady()` block (:332) register `powerMonitor.on('resume', …)` — there is no powerMonitor listener anywhere in the tree today — and route it to `SessionManager.runMissedRunSweep()`. Debounce so a resume immediately followed by the aligned minute tick cannot double-fire (the cursor already prevents a duplicate; the debounce prevents two sweeps racing the same write).

Call it when a catch-up run starts (desktop-scheduled-tasks.md:74, "Desktop shows a notification when a catch-up run starts"), with the automation name and the missed time. Note this is the plain host notification, not `deliverModelNotification` (:100), whose focus/presence gate belongs to the model-invocable PushNotification tool.

Table-driven against a fixed clock: daily `0 9 * * *` with a cursor six days old → exactly one fire at the most recent 9am and the cursor jumps past all six; occurrence older than seven days → no fire; cursor already equal to the occurrence → no re-fire; `enabled: false` → no fire; timezone matcher respected. Plus a schedule-state round-trip test (atomic write, corrupt file reads as empty).

blastRadius: Crosses a persistence boundary and probably the RPC boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. (1) New durable file in the managed workspace dir (~/.nessy/workspaces/<id>/automations-schedule-state.json), sibling to automations.json and automations-history.jsonl; nothing migrates it, but a corrupt/stale cursor is what decides whether a user's automation fires, so the read must fail closed. (2) `PromptHandler` refactor is on the path of EVERY App event (LabelAdd/…/SchedulerTick), covered by packages/shared/src/automations/handlers/prompt-handler.test.ts. (3) `AutomationSystem` has 14 callers (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts, lifecycle-hook-dispatcher.ts, index.ts) and tests automation-system.test.ts, task-hooks.test.ts, task-hook-decision.test.ts, hook-stdout-context.test.ts. (4) `matchesCron` has 6 callers including packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/plugin-monitor-service.ts — the new helper must be additive. (5) `PendingPrompt` gaining a `catchUp` field touches packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts and every construction site, and `executePromptAutomation` (SessionManager.ts:18542, interface at packages/server-core/src/handlers/session-manager-interface.ts:349) plus its tests (ephemeral-session.test.ts, execute-prompt-automation-nonblocking.test.ts). (6) If the wake sweep is invoked from electron main into server-core over RPC, add the channel in packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts, packages/shared/src/protocol/routing.ts and apps/electron/src/transport/channel-map.ts, and update apps/electron/src/shared/__tests__/ipc-channels.test.ts (that test enumerates channels). (7) The UI's `lastExecutedAt` (useAutomations.ts:54-64, AutomationsListPanel.tsx:138-146) will start showing catch-up runs as ordinary runs unless history entries mark them. (8) The powerMonitor listener is main-process code: per AGENTS.md, `electron:dev` will not pick it up, so live evidence needs a packaged build.
userImpact: Concrete and silent. A user creates a scheduled automation in the Automations UI — say cron `0 9 * * *` with a prompt action — and closes the laptop overnight. At 9am nothing happens. When they open the app at 11am, no session appears under the automation, no notification is shown, the card still reads "last ran" from whenever the machine last happened to be awake at 9am, and the run history has no entry at all — not even a skipped one — so there is nothing to tell them the run was lost. Claude Desktop would start exactly one catch-up session on wake and notify. Every scheduled automation whose cron time falls outside app uptime is affected, which for a daily-morning automation on a laptop is most days; the shorter the interval, the less it matters (an every-15-minutes task loses one occurrence and the next one arrives soon).
